2026-11-06.meal: Chicken gyros with tzatziki, slaw & sweet potato wedges
2026-11-06.note: Fakeaway Friday and this week's one meat night: kebab-shop feel, but air-fried with lots of salad. Gymnastics & swimming done earlier, nothing on for tea.

ingredients: 250g Greek yoghurt (half for the marinade, half for the tzatziki)
1 tsp smoked paprika, plus extra for the wedges
¼ red cabbage and 1 carrot, finely shredded
½ cucumber (half grated for the tzatziki, half sliced)
Sweet chilli sauce or chilli sauce, to serve (optional)
steps: Mix half the yoghurt with 1 garlic clove, the juice of half the lemon, the oregano, paprika, 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt. Stir the chicken through and leave it while you do the wedges (or marinate it in the fridge from the afternoon).
Heat the air fryer to 200°C. Toss the wedges in the rest of the oil, a pinch of paprika and salt, and air fry for 20 minutes, shaking halfway. Keep them warm.
Air fry the chicken thighs at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning halfway, until charred at the edges and cooked through with no pink in the middle.

Meanwhile, make the tzatziki: squeeze the grated cucumber dry and mix it with the rest of the yoghurt, the other garlic clove, a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt. Toss the cabbage and carrot with a squeeze of lemon for the slaw.
Rest the chicken for 2 minutes, then slice it into strips. Warm the flatbreads in the air fryer for 1 minute.
Fill the flatbreads with slaw, sliced cucumber, tomato and chicken, then add tzatziki and chilli sauce. Serve the wedges on the side.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: give her plain chicken strips, wedges and cucumber with plain yoghurt to dip. Leftover tzatziki is good for Sunday's picky tea.

2026-11-08.meal: Picky tea: crudités, dips & warm flatbreads
2026-11-08.note: Out for Sunday dinner, so just a light picky tea in the evening. Francis's away hockey fixture today.

ingredients: Carrots, cucumber and peppers, cut into sticks
Any leftover garlic yoghurt from Friday
steps: Cut the carrots, cucumber and peppers into sticks and put them on a big board with the cherry tomatoes.
Spoon the hummus and any leftover garlic yoghurt into bowls, and cube the cheese.
Warm the flatbreads in the air fryer at 180°C for 1–2 minutes, or in a dry pan, then cut them into strips for dipping.
Put everything in the middle and let everyone help themselves.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: cut her cherry tomatoes into quarters and her veg into thin sticks.

2026-11-09.meal: Sweet potato & spinach dhal with rice (double batch)
2026-11-09.note: Mathilda's hospital eye test this morning (off nursery) — a quiet one at home for the rest of the day, so a good evening to batch-cook extra for tomorrow's Hull hockey training. Alex now away for CYCLONE.

steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, lentils and stock. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils and sweet potato are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and spinach and cook for 3–4 minutes until the spinach wilts.
Take out Mathilda's portion and 4 portions to cool for Tuesday before seasoning the rest.
Cook the rice and serve with the dhal.
Cool the 4 extra portions within an hour, cover and keep in the fridge for Tuesday (no need to freeze).
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep hers plain and mash the sweet potato a little finer.

2026-11-10.meal: Reheat: Monday's sweet potato & spinach dhal with rice
2026-11-10.note: Hull hockey training 6–7pm (Hymers College) plus travel — tea ready for whoever's not driving, kept warm for the rest

ingredients: 4 portions of Monday's dhal (from the fridge)
steps: Tip the dhal into a pan with a splash of water.
Heat gently, stirring, until bubbling and piping hot all the way through (about 8–10 minutes). Or microwave in a covered bowl for 4–5 minutes, stirring halfway.
Cook the rice while the dhal heats.
Serve straightaway.
recipe.tip: Only reheat it once, and check it's piping hot all the way through before serving. Anyone back late from training can have theirs microwaved separately.

2026-11-11.meal: Air-fryer crispy gnocchi with roasted tomatoes, courgette & pesto
2026-11-11.note: Hockey Academy Night 6:15–7:45pm (The Lindum). Ready in 20 minutes either side of the run. (Swapped in because there's no Saturday curry in the freezer now.)

ingredients: Grated parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, to serve
steps: Heat the air fryer to 200°C.
Toss the gnocchi, courgette and cherry tomatoes in the oil with a pinch of salt.
Air fry for 12–15 minutes, shaking the basket every 5 minutes, until the gnocchi is golden and crisp and the tomatoes have burst. (Do it in two batches if your basket is small.)
Tip into a big bowl and toss with the pesto, and the spinach if using.
Serve with cheese on top.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: give her some plain crispy gnocchi and tomatoes before the pesto goes in, with a little cheese.

2026-11-12.note: Mathilda's Scotter Primary open day this morning — evening's free, nothing on for tea

ingredients: Zest of 1 lemon, plus a squeeze of juice
Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, to serve
steps: Cook the pasta according to the pack instructions, then drain, saving a mugful of the water.
Season the salmon and pan-fry for 3–4 minutes each side until just cooked through, then flake into chunks.
In a separate pan, soften the leek in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the peas and a splash of the pasta water, and cook for 2–3 minutes.
Stir in the crème fraîche and lemon zest, and warm through. Take out Mathilda's portion of sauce now if she's sensitive to lemon.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice to the rest, then toss the pasta through the sauce with the flaked salmon.
Serve with a sprinkle of cheese.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: flake her salmon extra small and check carefully for bones.
